spec.name: Calder Standing Mobile
spec.description: A Calder-style standing mobile: a black pedestal and curving stem carry a crown of sweeping wire arms from which three tiers of flat red, orange, yellow, white and black sheet-metal shapes hang in balanced suspension.
spec.layout: Front view (+Z): a low black pedestal disc sits on the floor at the origin; a slightly S-curved black stem rises 2.0 m to mount mastTop. From mastTop the wire crown sweeps one arm out left-forward to hookL [0.55, 1.94, 0.2] and one arm right-back to hookR [-0.5, 1.8, -0.1], with a short central branch bearing a small yellow triangle finial at the very top (~2.14). From each hook a thin vertical wire drop hangs the upper tier (canopy): on the left a big black leaf and a red petal, on the right a big white fan and a small orange disc; the drops continue down to pivotA (right-forward) and pivotB (left-back). The middle tier (midSwags) hangs from those pivots: an orange leaf forward-right and a black triangle behind it, a yellow half-moon and a small red disc to the left-back; the drops continue to pivotC and pivotD. The bottom tier (finials) hangs lowest: a large black blob-leaf on a balance arm with a solid counterweight sphere and a white disc at right-forward, and the model's boldest accent — a big red petal — with a yellow triangle and a single small cerulean disc at left-back. Lowest shape edges hover ~0.23 m above the floor; only the pedestal touches y = 0. Style on every part: nothing straight — every wire is one confident sweeping catmull curve in near-black; every shape is a flat cutout with visible 2-3 cm thickness so it reads as painted sheet metal seen both face-on and edge-on; hard-edged matte colours, asymmetric balance (heavy black mass left, bold red note right), black calligraphy lines holding coloured notes in the air.

parts.builds: The floor-standing base and stem, everything below mastTop [0, 2.0, 0]. The foot: b.lathe a low disc profile r 0.42, height 0.07, with a rounded lip and a shallow dome top, colour pedestal, resting on y = 0; on its top a small raised collar disc r 0.16, h 0.05, same colour, carrying a thin 2 mm white inlay ring (colour white) around its rim. The stem: b.sweep along catmull [[0,0.12,0],[0.025,0.7,0],[-0.02,1.35,0.02],[0,2.0,0]], radius [0.024, 0.015], colour wire — a gentle S-curve, never straight. A small side twig near the base: b.rod from the stem at [0.03, 0.5, 0.0] to [0.2, 0.52, 0.05], r 0.008, colour wire, carrying one tiny white oval leaf (b.extrude outline ~0.10 x 0.16, smoothing 2, thickness 0.02, colour white, facing mostly +Z tilted ~20 degrees) — a quiet Calder whisper near the ground. At mastTop the stem ends in a tiny upturned hook: a half-torus (tube r 0.005, ring r 0.018, colour wire) opening upward, so the armature's attachment ring hangs in it; both parts build their meeting hardware at mastTop.
parts.attaches: Rises to mount mastTop [0, 2.0, 0], where the armature's ring hangs in the stem's terminal hook.

parts.builds: The black wire crown above the stem, from mastTop [0, 2.0, 0]. Two main curved arms, each one b.sweep along a catmull, colour wire: the left arm r 0.014 from [0, 2.0, 0] rising through [0.12, 2.06, 0.04] and curving out left-forward to hookL [0.55, 1.94, 0.2]; the right arm r 0.013 from [0, 2.0, 0] through [-0.14, 2.07, -0.03] curving out right-back to hookR [-0.5, 1.8, -0.1]. A short central branch up to [0, 2.12, 0.01] carrying the crown finial: a small yellow triangle (b.extrude outline ~0.09 per side, thickness 0.02, colour yellow, facing +Z). At hookL and hookR each arm ends in a closed attachment ring: b.part TorusGeometry(0.02, 0.005) in the vertical plane of the coming drop, colour wire — the canopy's top wire loops through it. Two small spacer spheres r 0.012 (colour wire) seated on the arms at mid-span. Style: every arm a single confident curved line, no straight segments, the whole crown reading as black calligraphy against the air.
parts.attaches: Roots at mount mastTop [0, 2.0, 0] on the stem's terminal hook; ends at mounts hookL and hookR with its closed rings, which the canopy hangs from.

parts.builds: The upper tier of hanging sheet shapes, suspended from hookL [0.55, 1.94, 0.2] and hookR [-0.5, 1.8, -0.1]. Left drop: b.sweep along catmull from hookL down through [0.62, 1.75, 0.22] to mount pivotA [0.85, 1.45, 0.3], r 0.010, colour wire, ending in a small closed ring (torus 0.016 / 0.004, colour wire) for the next tier. On it, short twigs (r 0.006, colour wire) carry: a big black leaf — b.extrude an organic 3-4 point outline ~0.34 wide x 0.50 tall, smoothing 2, thickness 0.03, colour sheetBlack — hung at [0.78, 1.62, 0.26], facing mostly +Z tilted ~25 degrees; a red petal ~0.20 x 0.28, thickness 0.025, colour red, at [0.58, 1.78, 0.12], facing forward with a slight jaunty tilt. Right drop: b.sweep from hookR down through [-0.62, 1.5, -0.03] to mount pivotB [-0.8, 1.25, -0.05], r 0.010, ring at pivotB. On it: a big white fan/petal ~0.30 x 0.40, thickness 0.028, colour white, at [-0.55, 1.58, -0.02], facing forward-right (normal ~[0.4, 0, 0.85]); a small orange disc r 0.09, thickness 0.03, colour orange, at [-0.4, 1.72, 0.02], facing mostly +Z. Spacer balls r 0.012 (colour wire) where twigs join the drops. Every shape hangs with its own slight tilt; no two planes coplanar, so edges and faces alternate down the tier.
parts.attaches: Hangs from mounts hookL and hookR (the armature's rings) and ends at mounts pivotA and pivotB, where midSwags hangs below.

parts.builds: The middle tier, hanging from pivotA [0.85, 1.45, 0.3] and pivotB [-0.8, 1.25, -0.05]. Left branch: b.sweep along catmull [0.85,1.45,0.3] -> [0.7,1.15,0.35] -> [0.6,1.02,0.33] -> pivotC [0.55,0.85,0.15], r 0.009, colour wire, small closed ring at pivotC. Twigs (r 0.006): a big orange leaf — organic outline ~0.30 x 0.42, thickness 0.03, smoothing 2, colour orange — hung at [0.72, 0.92, 0.45] on a forward twig, facing +Z tilted ~20 degrees; a small black triangle ~0.16 per side, thickness 0.025, colour sheetBlack, at [0.48, 1.08, 0.12] on a backward twig, angled ~40 degrees off +Z. Right branch: b.sweep along catmull [-0.8,1.25,-0.05] -> [-0.6,1.0,0.0] -> pivotD [-0.45,0.7,-0.1], r 0.009, ring at pivotD. Twigs: a yellow half-moon ~0.26 x 0.30, thickness 0.028, colour yellow, at [-0.55, 0.95, 0.02], facing +Z with a slight roll; a small red disc r 0.07, thickness 0.025, colour red, at [-0.85, 1.08, -0.18], facing forward-left. Spacer balls r 0.010 at twig junctions, colour wire.
parts.attaches: Hangs from mounts pivotA and pivotB (the canopy's rings) and ends at mounts pivotC and pivotD, where finials hangs below.

parts.builds: The bottom tier, hanging from pivotC [0.55, 0.85, 0.15] and pivotD [-0.45, 0.7, -0.1]. Right cluster: b.sweep from pivotC down to [0.55, 0.55, 0.18], r 0.008, colour wire, then a gentle horizontal balance arm r 0.008 from [0.42, 0.52, 0.16] to [0.72, 0.5, 0.24]; at its left end a solid black counterweight sphere r 0.05 (colour wire); from the arm's middle a 0.06 twig holds a large black blob-leaf — rounded organic outline ~0.40 x 0.34, thickness 0.032, smoothing 2, colour sheetBlack — at [0.55, 0.42, 0.2], facing +Z tilted ~15 degrees; another twig up to a small white disc r 0.06, thickness 0.02, colour white, at [0.7, 0.62, 0.3]. Left cluster: b.sweep from pivotD down to [-0.4, 0.45, -0.06], r 0.008; the model's boldest accent: a big red petal — organic outline ~0.30 wide x 0.34 tall, thickness 0.03, smoothing 2, colour red — at [-0.42, 0.40, -0.04], facing mostly +Z tilted ~30 degrees; a twig up to a small yellow triangle ~0.14 per side, thickness 0.02, colour yellow, at [-0.58, 0.52, -0.14]; a tiny cerulean disc r 0.045, thickness 0.02, colour cerulean, at [-0.28, 0.5, 0.02] — the single blue note in the whole composition. All shape bottoms stay at or above y = 0.23, floating free of the pedestal top.
parts.attaches: Hangs from mounts pivotC and pivotD (the midSwags rings); nothing below it, its shapes hover ~0.23 m above the floor.

Thinking Process:

1.  **Analyze the Request:** The user wants me to generate a JSON specification for a complex object (a hanging mobile) that will be built collaboratively by multiple builders using an external SDK (`agentic-3js-builder`).
2.  **Analyze the Subject & Style:**
    *   **Subject:** Hanging mobile.
    *   **Category:** Abstract.
    *   **Style:** Alexander Calder (fluid, balanced, kinetic, minimal forms, often contrasting shapes).
3.  **Determine Scale and Structure (Calder Mobile):**
    *   A mobile needs a central hanging point and several articulated arms with various shapes.
    *   Dimensions: Needs to be large enough to look significant, but abstract. Let's aim for a moderate size.
    *   The structure should involve several interconnected elements: a main hanging ring/bar, and several arms/shapes suspended from it.
    *   We need 3-6 parts. A mobile can be divided into:
        1.  Main suspension structure (the top bar/ring).
        2.  The main arms/structural elements.
        3.  The suspended abstract shapes (the "blobs").
        4.  Small decorative/counterbalancing elements.
4.  **Define Constraints & Parameters:**
    *   `size`: Overall dimensions (X, Y, Z). Let's estimate X=3m, Y=3m, Z=3m for a balanced, spreading mobile.
    *   `layout`: How the mobile spreads out (e.g., flat against the X-Z plane, suspended at Y=H/2).
    *   `palette`: Needs a few distinct, bold, flat colors suitable for a minimalist/abstract art piece.
    *   `mount`s: The primary hanging point.
    *   `joints`: The skeletal structure (pivots, connections).
    *   `parts`: The geometry groups.

5.  **Develop the Structure (Joint/Skeleton first):**
    *   Root: Central hanging point (`body`).
    *   Arms: Several arms hang from the `body`.
    *   Elements: Shapes hang from the ends of the arms.

6.  **Fleshing out the JSON (Iterative design):**

    *   **Size:** [3.0, 3.0, 3.0] (X, Y, Z)
    *   **Palette:** Needs contrasting, appealing colors. Perhaps muted tones with a pop of bright color.
        *   `hull`: Muted gray/metal (#A0A0A0)
        *   `shape1`: Bright primary (Yellow/Orange #FFD700)
        *   `shape2`: Cool primary (Cyan/Blue #00BFFF)
        *   `detail`: Dark contrasting line/core (#222222)
    *   **Layout:** Focus on X-Z plane expansion, centered at Y=0 (or a fixed suspension height). Since it's a hanging mobile, the root won't rest on the floor (`floor: false` implicitly for everything).
    *   **Mount:** The single point where it's hung.
    *   **Joint:** The main pivot structure.

7.  **Refining Parts (6 parts for even split):**

    *   P1: Suspension Hardware (The top connector/ring).
    *   P2: Primary Arms (The main structural pieces).
    *   P3: Large Abstract Shapes (The dominant visual elements).
    *   P4: Secondary Arms/Connectors (Smaller supports).
    *   P5: Small Elements/Ornaments (Counterbalances).
    *   P6: Background/Connecting elements (If necessary, but let's stick to the mobile components).

8.  **Final Review against Prompt Requirements:**
    *   JSON format only.
    *   `name`, `description`, `builderName` (must be camelCase).
    *   `size`, `layout`, `palette`, `mount`s, `joints`, `parts` structure is correct.
    *   Style adherence (Calder: Abstract, balanced, simple forms, kinetic feel).

*(Self-Correction during drafting: Ensure the joints are defined before parts use them. The mobile structure must be purely defined by its joints.)*

Let's assemble the final JSON.The user wants me to design a shared specification (a JSON object) for a multi-builder system to create a single model.
The model is a "hanging mobile" in the style of "Alexander Calder."
The style dictates bold, readable, stylized shapes, low-poly look, and clear color palettes.
The model must be built using primitive shapes and the SDK constraints (flat colors, etc.).

Since it's a "hanging mobile," there will be several suspended parts connected by wires or arms, creating dynamic, abstract shapes.

**Model Analysis (Calder Mobile):**
1.  **Structure:** A central hanging point (top) and several suspended elements (wings, flat shapes, kinetic elements).
2.  **Shape:** Abstract, biomorphic, often utilizing simple, recognizable forms (circles, ovals, thin rectangles) but rendered in a dynamic composition.
3.  **Style:** Use of balance, movement, and color contrast. Low-poly, stylized.

**Translating to Specification:**
*   **Name/Description:** Hanging Mobile, Abstract Calder style.
*   **Size:** Needs to fit the scope of a large mobile, perhaps 1.5m wide, 2m high, 0.5m deep.
*   **Layout:** The primary structure is a central suspension point, and the elements hang down and out.
*   **Palette:** Needs colors suitable for a stylized abstract sculpture. Maybe contrasting, bold, flat colors.
*   **Mounts/Joints:** The primary joint will be the central suspension point. The moving elements are attached via thin rods/wires (which act as joints/chains).
*   **Parts:** I'll define 3-4 major parts:
    1.  The central suspension apparatus/arm structure.
    2.  A large, flat upper plate/wing (Part 1).
    3.  A suspended, detailed kinetic cluster (Part 2).
    4.  A final, small, whimsical element (Part 3).

Let's refine the dimensions and structure.

**Dimensions:**
*   Width (X): ~1.8m (to spread the arms)
*   Height (Y): ~2.0m (from central suspension point down)

*   Overall Size: `[1.8, 2.0, 1.0]`

**Colors:**
*   A few contrasting, bold colors.
*   `hull`: A neutral/dark color for the structure (e.g., dark grey/bronze).

**Joint Structure:**
*   A main anchor point (off-screen, top of the builder's object). Let's define a `root` joint for the entire assembly's attachment point.

**Parts Definition:**

1.  **Center/Suspension Hub:** The core piece from which all elements hang.
2.  **Upper Wing:** A large, flat, stylized plate.

I need to ensure the descriptions are detailed enough for multiple builders to interpret them as one cohesive model based on the shared vision.

---
**Drafting the JSON:**The user wants me to design a shared specification (JSON format) for building a model, specifically a hanging mobile in the style of Alexander Calder.

The final output must be a JSON specification, not the actual three.js module.
The model needs to be split into 3-6 parts.

**Model Description:**
*   **Category:** Abstract
*   **Subject:** Hanging mobile (Alexander Calder style).
*   **Style:** Abstract, Calder-esque (dynamic, balanced, simple geometric forms, usually hanging with wires/arms).

**Design Considerations for Calder Mobile:**
1.  **Structure:** It needs a central hanging point (arm/suspension).
2.  **Shapes:** Simple, planar, often asymmetric shapes (circles, ovals, lenticular, geometric abstractions).
3.  **Balance:** Visual weight and balance are crucial.
4.  **Movement:** The parts imply movement and delicate suspension.
5.  **Palette:** Limited, bold, contrasting colors.

**Constraints Check:**
*   Output: Single JSON block. No external text.
*   Structure: `name`, `description`, `builderName`, `size`, `layout`, `palette`, `mount`, `joints`, `parts`.
*   `parts`: 3-6 parts, self-contained, budget divided.
*   `palette`: Max 24 colors.
*   `joints`: Skeleton definition.
*   `box`: Min/Max corners.

**Plan:**
1.  Define overall size and layout for a mobile.
2.  Define the skeleton (joints) for the suspension mechanism.
3.  Divide the mobile into 3-4 distinct parts: Central Arm/Suspension, Large Primary Elements, Medium Secondary Elements, and Small Accent Elements.
4.  Assign a palette.

**Execution:**

**1. Size and Layout:**
A mobile needs enough vertical space and lateral swing. Let's aim for a manageable size, say 2m tall, 2m wide, and depth determined by the arm length.

**2. Joints:**
The root must be the hanging point. Subsequent joints attach to the primary arms.

*   `root` (The main suspension point).
*   `arm1` (Primary structural element 1, attached to root).
*   `arm2` (Primary structural element 2, attached to root).
*   `element1` (Attaches to `arm1`).
*   `element2` (Attaches to `arm2`).

Let's simplify the joints for the JSON spec, focusing on the attachment points for the parts.

**3. Palette:**
We need bold, Calder-like contrasts.
*   Primary: Bright Cyan (`#00BFFF`), Red (`#FF4500`), Yellow (`#FFFF00`).
*   Secondary/Structural: Matte Grey (`#AAAAAA`), Dark Navy (`#1A237E`).

**4. Parts Definition (Target 4 parts for good division):**

*   **Part 1: Main Suspension Arm (The central boom).** Defines the structure holding everything.
*   **Part 2: Large Primary Element (The biggest shape, defining the main plane).**
*   **Part 3: Medium Cluster (A group of smaller, swinging shapes).**
*   **Part 4: Accent/Counterbalance (A small, delicate element).**

Let's refine the coordinates and budgets.

*   Total Budget: 900 parts. Let's target ~225 parts per main part.

*(Self-Correction during drafting: Since it's an abstract mobile, the joints are more like attachment points on arms, not traditional skeletal movement. I will define the primary suspension structure as the core system.)*

**Finalizing the JSON structure:**The user wantsI need to write a spec for a Calder hanging mobile. The builders will build one part each. A Calder mobile: a hanging kinetic sculpture with black flat shapes (organic leaf-like and geometric shapes), red/orange/yellow accents, thin black rods, suspended from a ceiling... but the model stands on y=0 floor? "A model the pitch places off the ground (a bird in flight, a hanging lantern) keeps that height." So the mobile hangs — but where does it hang from? A mobile needs a mount point. In a model space, we could hang it from a tall thin pole/stand (Calder made standing mobiles too — "stabiles" are static; "standing mobiles" exist). A standing mobile on a base would let it rest on the floor and be fully self-contained. That's a good choice: a Calder standing mobile — a black base, a vertical stem, curving black wire arms, with painted shapes (black, red, orange, yellow, white) suspended.

Size: maybe 2.2 m tall, width 2.0 m, depth 0.7 m. Size [2.0, 2.2, 0.9].

Split into 3-6 parts: 
1. base + stem (mast): black base cylinder, vertical stem, maybe with a white/red stripe? Calder base is usually black. Budget ~120.
2. the upper wire tree / armature: curved black rods branching out — first tier arms. Budget ~150.
3. lower branch cluster (left side shapes + connecting wires): shapes hanging on wires with small wire connectors, spacers. Budget ~200.
4. middle cluster. Budget ~200.
5. right/top cluster. Budget ~200.

Total ~870.

Joints: static model? A mobile is kinetic but we can have joints for rotation — actually joints could be nice for animation (each mobile tier rotating slowly). The rig: joints at pivot points for each arm so it can sway. But spec says static models may omit joints. For a mobile, having joints at each pivot would be great for a rig that animates the rotation. Let's include joints: root at base? A static model has "joints": []. But a mobile that rotates is a good candidate for joints. Let me define:

- root "base" at [0, 0, 0], dir [0,1,0] — hmm, root joint. Actually the mast could sway? Keep base static.
- "mast" at [0, 0.12, 0] dir [0,1,0] — the stem, so a gentle sway is possible.
- Pivot joints at each arm branch point: "pivotTop" etc. Each cluster hangs from a pivot and can rotate about vertical axis. That's the classic mobile motion — rotation about the vertical wire axis. So joints at each vertical hanging point, dir [0,1,0], role "hinge".

Let me lay out geometry. Standing mobile, 2.2 m tall:

- Base: black disc/cylinder r=0.42, h=0.06, at floor. Plus a smaller pedestal disc r=0.18, h=0.10.
- Mast: vertical black rod from y=0.16 to y=2.05, r=0.025, tapering. Maybe slightly curved (Calder stems often curve). Let's make it a catmull curve leaning slightly.
- Top of mast at ~2.0. From there arms branch.

Armature structure (wire tree): 
From mast top (~2.0), a curved arm sweeps forward-left to about [0.55, 1.85, 0.25], with a hanging point. Another arm sweeps right to [-0.6, 1.7, -0.1]. Classic Calder:不平衡 balance with counterweights.

Structure plan (three tiers):

Tier A (top, y≈1.85–2.1): from mast top, a horizontal-ish curved arm crossing left-to-right; at each end a vertical wire drops to a shape or a second-tier pivot.

Tier B (middle, y≈1.2–1.6): two sub-arms each carrying shapes and a lower pivot.

Tier C (lower, y≈0.4–1.0): shapes directly hanging.

Shapes: flat organic cutouts, thickness ~0.02–0.04, standing vertically (planes roughly vertical, facing various directions), like Calder's sheet metal leaves and petals, and some geometric (circle, triangle, half-moon). Colors: mostly black, with red, orange, yellow, white accents (Calder palette: black, white, red, orange, yellow).

Let me define mounts:
- mastTop: [0, 2.0, 0] — where stem ends and armature begins.
- pivotL / pivotR: where first-tier arms end and vertical drops hang... Actually the drops belong to clusters.
- Mounts are where two parts touch. Parts: mast (base+stem), armature (wire tree first tier), clusterLeft, clusterRight, clusterLower? Let me use 5 parts:

1. "pedestal" — base + stem. Owns floor. Budget 120.
2. "armature" — the crown: curved arms from mastTop, first-tier horizontal wires, ending in hanging points with small rings/hooks. Mount: mastTop. Budget 160.
3. "canopy" — top tier: shapes hanging directly from armature hooks (big leaf shapes + small counterweights), plus its own sub-wires and drops to middle pivots. Mount: armature hooks (armHookL, armHookR). Budget 190.
4. "midSwags" — middle tier: arms/pivots with shapes and drops to lower hooks. Budget 200.
5. "finials" — bottom tier: final shapes, counterweight spheres/discs, small spacers. Budget 180.

Hmm, that's reasonable. Mounts: mastTop [0, 2.0, 0]; hookL [0.55, 1.92, 0.22]; hookR [-0.5, 1.78, -0.12]; pivotMidL, pivotMidR, pivotLowL, pivotLowR... Mounts are shared points where parts meet; each place two parts touch has a mount. So:

- mastTop [0, 2.0, 0] — pedestal ↔ armature.
- hookL [0.55, 1.94, 0.2] — armature ↔ canopy (canopy hangs from this).
- hookR [-0.5, 1.8, -0.1] — armature ↔ canopy.
- pivotA [0.85, 1.45, 0.3] — canopy ↔ midSwags (mid part hangs from canopy's sub-wire).
- pivotB [-0.8, 1.25, -0.05] — canopy ↔ midSwags.
- pivotC [0.55, 0.85, 0.15] — midSwags ↔ finials.
- pivotD [-0.45, 0.7, -0.1] — midSwags ↔ finials.

Parts boxes: since it's hanging, boxes are generous regions:
- pedestal: [[-0.45, 0, -0.45], [0.45, 2.0, 0.45]]
- armature: [[-0.7, 1.7, -0.35], [0.75, 2.2, 0.45]]
- canopy: [[-1.0, 1.15, -0.4], [1.05, 2.0, 0.55]]
- midSwags: [[-1.0, 0.55, -0.45], [1.05, 1.55, 0.5]]
- finials: [[-0.85, 0.25, -0.35], [0.9, 0.95, 0.4]]

Total size: width 2.1, height 2.2, depth 0.9. Size [2.1, 2.2, 0.9].

Joints: root at base? For a static model joints: []. But a mobile wants rotating tiers. Let's give joints:

- "stem" at [0, 0.16, 0], dir [0,1,0], role spine, parent none (root). Rides: pedestal. Hmm — root joint must be first. The stem joint is the root; everything hangs from chain... Actually if I make a joint chain, the armature could sway slightly. Simple set:
- "stem" (root) at [0,0.16,0] dir [0,1,0] role spine
- "pivotL" at hookL, dir [0,1,0], role hinge, parent stem — canopy left cluster rotates about vertical.
- "pivotR" at hookR, dir [0,1,0], role hinge, parent stem
- "pivotA" at pivotA, parent pivotL, role hinge
- "pivotB" at pivotB, parent pivotR, role hinge
- "pivotC" at pivotC, parent pivotA, role hinge
- "pivotD" at pivotD, parent pivotB, role hinge

That's 7 joints. Each part lists which joints its geometry rides: armature rides "stem"; canopy rides pivotL/pivotR; midSwags rides pivotA/pivotB; finials rides pivotC/pivotD.

Wait — the parent chain: pivotA is at [0.85, 1.45, 0.3] and its parent is pivotL at [0.55,1.94,0.2]. Bone direction from parent to child... The joint's dir is the bone direction. For a hanging pivot, dir [0,1,0] means the bone points up — but the child is below. Hmm, bones point from joint to children. Actually in the SDK, the joint's bone is +Y of the joint and children joints... the dir is where the bone points. For a hanging pivot, the geometry hangs below, so maybe dir should be [0,-1,0] pointing down toward the hanging weight? The bone runs from a joint to each child joint. Child pivotA is below pivotL, so the bone direction from pivotL to pivotA is downward: dir [0,-1,0]... Actually pivotL's children could be geometry hanging below (canopy shapes attached to this pivot via the vertical wire). Let me just set dir [0,-1,0] for the hanging pivots, so the +Y axis points down toward the hanging cluster — makes sense for "hinge" pivots that carry the drop below.

Hmm, but actually, for rotating about the vertical wire, the joint axis is vertical. Three.js rotation is about the joint's Y axis. So dir [0,1,0] or [0,-1,0] both give vertical rotation axis. dir defines the bone direction to children. For pivots whose child is below, dir [0,-1,0]. For stem (root), children are the armature at the top and pivots... The armature is at mastTop [0,2.0,0], above stem. So stem's dir [0,1,0] pointing up to the armature. Good.

Actually wait: does the armature ride "stem" joint? The armature is rigid with the stem — both belong to the static top. Fine.

Should the pedestal be part of the stem joint? The root joint at [0,0.16,0] — base disc is below it. Static model might be simpler, but joints give animation potential (rotating tiers = mobile motion). I'll include them.
